A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Bilevel-ZOFO research. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices support reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original single-task fine-tuning, meta-learning, prompt-sensitivity, ablation, and resource measurements in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains original experiments and adds design comparisons, full first-order baselines, math/code evaluations, and DePT results.

M1.justification: Algorithm 1 corrects its outer updates to use the newly computed auxiliary state s^(k+1), rather than s^k, aligning the pseudocode with the existing explanation. The proposed Algorithm 2 retains its penalty objective, SPSA backbone updates, and first-order PEFT updates; no changed experimental implementation is established.

E1.justification: V2 adds mathematical reasoning and code-generation coverage through GSM8K, Math500, and HumanEval, including prompted versus raw-format GSM8K evaluation. The existing classification, question-answering, and four meta-learning scenarios remain. Proposed future applications are not evaluated.

E2.justification: V2 adds Bilevel-ZOZO and joint-optimization comparators in Table 5, full first-order fine-tuning in Tables 11-12, and DePT in Table 15. It also extends the previously COPA-only two-stage comparison to BoolQ, CB, and SST2. Existing principal comparator sets are retained.

E3.justification: New Qwen2-7B experiments specify 2,000 LoRA/Bilevel-ZOFO steps versus 10,000 MeZO steps, a 4:1 Math500 split, and accuracy/pass@1 metrics. V2 also adds data-split sensitivity testing. For existing experiments, Appendix D.1 changes 20 inner updates to 10, matching the already-stated main-text setting; this does not establish rerunning.

E4.justification: V2 adds tests separating the benefits of exact PEFT gradients and bilevel optimization from ZO-only and joint optimization (Table 5), a lower/upper data-ratio ablation (Figure 4c), and GSM8K prompt robustness (Table 13). The earlier penalty, inner-step, and two-stage analyses remain.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed means and standard deviations for the main single-task experiments, five test seeds for meta-learning, and three-run timing averages. V2 introduces no additional uncertainty-estimation procedure or explicit increase in repeated runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds design-control, full-FO, math/code, DePT, and resource results. Existing OPT and meta-learning scores and detailed uncertainty tables are retained. Table 3 corrects the Bilevel-ZOFO BoolQ average from 0.7937 to 0.8270; Table 9 revises its COPA entry from 76.66 to 76.33. The parameter-count results in v1 Figure 3 are omitted. New benchmark results do not establish improvements over v1 under identical settings.

T1.justification: V1 Section 5 and Appendix A reappear as v2 Appendices B-C with the same assumptions, stationarity definitions, convergence theorem, complexity bounds, and proofs. Renumbering, notation clarification, and the new explanatory caveat about strong convexity do not change the formal analysis.

C1.justification: The central hybrid-method, convergence, accuracy, memory-efficiency, and meta-learning claims remain. V2 adds an explicit 2-4x training/time-to-target claim and an abstract-level claim that inner adaptation reduces ZO-estimate variance, while specifying the memory-constrained target setting more clearly.

C2.justification: V2 adds interpretations of the joint/ZO-only controls and data-split results, explicitly qualifies the strong-convexity assumption, and acknowledges that very large LLMs were not tested. It also discusses task choice and future applications. Much of the earlier explanation of prompt sensitivity, noisy ZO updates, and bilevel guidance is retained.

D1.justification: V2 removes v1's explicit LoRA rank 8/scaling 16, five-prefix-token, and ten-soft-prompt-token settings. It adds brief Qwen2-7B training details, identifies LoRA in the prompt-sensitivity experiment, and promises future code release without providing access. Most optimizer, hardware, precision, and learning-rate information remains.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations to DePT, AutoPrompt, Ji et al.'s bilevel analysis, and Mackay et al.'s self-tuning networks, while removing the Levesque and Rajpurkar dataset references. Its principal positioning against MeZO, FO-PEFT, and existing bilevel methods remains; much related work is relocated.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and contribution statement are substantially rewritten. V2 subdivides the method and experimental narrative, places ablations before meta-learning, condenses main-text related work, and moves the theoretical analysis into the appendices. It also adds limitations and a conference checklist.

P2.justification: V2 changes the main document from two-column to single-column layout, adds the eight-panel accuracy/runtime/memory Figure 1, expands the ablation figure, and adds comparison tables. It expands the meta-learning table with resource columns, relocates several existing displays, and removes the parameter-count figure.

improvement.justification: The new ZOZO and joint-optimization controls strengthen evidence for the bilevel design, while full-FO comparisons and resource measurements make its tradeoffs easier to assess. Explicit limitations also improve calibration. These gains are tempered by removed PEFT hyperparameters and briefly specified math/code protocols, leaving a limited net improvement in evidential support and clarity.
